subject: Material selection for reliable manufacture
hook: Mark the grain, or the doors won't match.
ig:
Mark the grain, or the doors won't match. One column on a cutting list saves a re-cut.

Plain decors don't care which way a part is cut from the sheet. Woodgrain decors do. The grain runs along the length of the board, and if your list doesn't say which dimension follows it, parts can get rotated to nest better on the sheet.

The result: a tall door with vertical grain next to an end panel with horizontal grain. Nobody's happy.

The fix is simple:
— add a grain column to your cutting list
— mark which dimension runs with the grain on every woodgrain part
— flag any parts that need to match across a run, like a bank of drawer fronts

It's one of the first things we check when a cut-and-edge order comes in.

What's the cutting-list mistake you see most often? Tell us below, and save this for your next order.
fb:
A quick one for the trade: if you're ordering cut and edged boards in a woodgrain decor, mark the grain direction on your cutting list.

Without it, parts can be rotated to fit the sheet better, and you end up with a door and an end panel running in different directions. A grain column, and a note on any parts that need to match across a run, sorts it.
